constraint_decided_it: P14's own scope note declares P14.1 in the role of as the construct that 'specifies the nature of an Actor's participation' (example: painting of the Sistine Chapel carried out by Michelangelo in the role of master craftsman), and E13's scope note names P177 assigned property of type (E13 -> E55, with the note that CRM properties are themselves instances of E55 Type) as the way to state which property an assignment asserts. B uses both; A uses neither, and A additionally omits P128 carries (E18 -> E90), so A's E33 text is never attached to the E22 letters and no path in A's model connects any actor to the signature at all.
better_modelling: Composition: E65 Creation, P94 has created (E65 -> E28; E33 is a subclass of E28 via E73/E89) the E33 Linguistic Object, P14 carried out by the clerk with P14.1 in the role of 'drafter', that single P14 claim reified as E13 Attribute Assignment (P140 -> the E65, P141 -> the unnamed E21, P177 -> P14 as E55 Type, P3 has note for the handwriting/letterhead evidence). Signing should be its own act, not a role on the creation of the text: an E11 Modification (or E7 Activity typed 'signing') P14 carried out by the secretary, P31 has modified (E11 -> E18) the E22 letter, which P128 carries the E33 text and P65 shows visual item the signature. For a legible name-text the signature is more specifically an E34 Inscription (subclass of both E33 and E37, 'recognisable texts attached to instances of E24') than a bare E37 Mark.
reasoning: Every property in both answers respects its declared domain and range (P94 E65->E28 with E33 subsumed under E28; P14 E7->E39 with E65 a subclass of E7; P65 E24->E36 with E22/E37; P140/P141 E13->E1; P177 E13->E55), so neither is wrong, but neither reached the most specific construct on both halves. A is the weaker: it drops P14.1, the property the CRM declares for exactly the drafter/signatory split, drops P177 from its E13 so the assignment never says which property is being asserted, never links the E33 to the E22 with P128, and ends with no CRM path stating that the secretary signed anything; its plea of SIG indeterminacy (t0796 'Modeling relationships with multiple roles', unresolved; t1477, unresolved) is genuine about reification-vs-sub-event patterns but does not excuse skipping a declared property. B loses points for hanging the 'signatory' role off the E65 Creation of the text, contradicting its own rejected alternative that signing produces no new conceptual content, where a separate E11 Modification/P31 on the physical letter is the direct construct, and for saying the generic '.2' certainty property was 'explicitly not adopted' when t1035 and t1263/Issue 349 show it merely left Open with no consensus. B's citations otherwise verify: the t1263 quote 'E13 introduces an additional agency, and is computationally heavy, as all reification-equivalent constructs' is verbatim Martin Doerr, Issue 349 Belief Values is Open, and A's paraphrase of P94 ('the composition of a poem, not its commitment to paper') is likewise accurate.
